pageCache.pageTitle: Al Madina School For Girls – Located in the heart of Barking, Al-Madina School for Girls (ASG) is an independent faith-based school that strives to foster an environment where academic excellence and Islamic values go hand in hand.
pageCache.text:
Welcome to Al-Madina School for Girls (ASG)
Located in the heart of Barking, Al-Madina School for Girls (ASG) is an independent faith-based school that strives to foster an environment where academic excellence and Islamic values go hand in hand. Our school was set up in September 2023 with the aim of providing an excellent education for girls from the ages of 11 to 16, placing particular emphasis on the building of good character, acquiring skills and instilling value for learning. We are committed to nurturing young minds, empowering girls to embrace their innate potential, and guiding them to become respectful, ambitious, and responsible individuals.
The ASG core values are rooted in the Islamic concept of ‘fitra’, the primordial state of inherent goodness and morality. We aim to develop pupils into individuals who embody the qualities of being Forbearing, Inquisitive, Truthful, Respectful, and Ambitious—qualities that are believed to be essential for personal growth and success. These core values are not only reflected in the curriculum but also in the way support is available for students’ character development, ensuring they grow into strong, confident, and compassionate leaders of tomorrow.
At Al-Madina School for Girls, we don’t just educate; we nurture hearts and minds, preparing students to excel academically and spiritually, and to make meaningful contributions to society. Join us as we embark on a journey of learning, growth, and excellence, guided by the light of fitra.

pageCache.pageTitle: Ethos & Core Values – Al Madina School For Girls
pageCache.text:
Ethos & Core Values
Executive Principal's Welcome
It is my great pleasure to announce on behalf of ASG – and its community of parents, pupils and stakeholders – the official publication of the ASG’s core values. The acronym FITRA stands for Forbearing; Inquisitive; Truthful; Respectful; and Ambitious. These represent the qualities we seek to instil and inculcate in our pupils. These qualities are described in Islamic teachings as virtuous attributes, each of which, are connected to the Islamic concept of ‘fitra’, described in Islamic literature – among other things – as being the primordial nature of the individual, namely, the state of inherent goodness, purity and innocence, and the individuals’ internal desire to be morally upright.
Abbas Aziz, BA (Hons), MScExecutive Principal

pageCache.pageTitle: Newsletter – Al Madina School For Girls
pageCache.text:
Newsletter
ASG News
We are exceptionally proud of all pupils who achieved a STAR Award, and thus, consistently demonstrate excellence in each and/or all the categories listed above, Al-hamdulillah. On behalf of Mr Aziz, we extend our sincere thanks to parents of these pupils for supporting your child/ren to demonstrate excellence in personal conduct and for being committed to the pursuit of knowledge.
At the conclusion of last year, the ASG had the pleasure of hosting a special visit to the school by Mufti Menk. In keeping with the school’s efforts to encourage and motivate our pupils through visits by external speakers, we had the great pleasure of announcing school visit by Ms S. Sesay, Vice Principal of Langdon Academy (part of the Brampton Manor Trust) and a former pupil, intended to inspire our pupils to strive to achieve excellence in accordance with the school’s vision. She shared her journey emigrating from Sierra Leonne with very little educational opportunity to becoming a senior leader in secondary education in mainstream UK schools. The whole school community was inspired by Ms Sesay’s visit. Ms.Sesay was herself inspired by the school and its work, so much so, that she has stated a desire to return for another visit in the future.
Our wonderful ex-pupil held a motivational session with year 11’s where she presented her experience of ASG in her final year (2024-25) as a year 11 pupil, and her GCSE success. She provided excellent practical tips on how to cope with the stress and pressure of year 11 and how to approach GCSE revision and exams. Her insights were extremely helpful and very well received by pupils. We extend our sincere thanks to Ms. Sesay and our former pupil for taking time out to visit ASG and to help motivate and encourage our pupils towards high achievement. We would also like to thank Ms Saleha for her efforts in securing the visits and for working with local schools to build partnerships and networks for the benefit of ASG pupils.
